---
title: "Server Manual"
subtitle: "SimilaritySearchServer: the REST API, the job queue and the two command lines"
lang: en-US
---

`SimilaritySearchServer` provides access to [`SimilaritySearchEngine`](../index.qmd), the
embedded engine documented in the rest of this site, through a REST API, two command lines and
an asynchronous job queue. It implements no indexing logic. **Storage, indexing and search are
implemented in the engine.** This package translates HTTP requests and command lines into
engine calls, and engine results and failures into responses and exit codes.

This division determines where each subject is documented. Questions about projects,
persistence, text profiles or the behavior of a search are answered in the engine's
[architecture guide](../architecture.qmd). The two packages are documented on one site because
the interface between them is the public API of the engine, and both sides of that interface
are described here.

## 1. What this package contains

| file | what it does |
| :--- | :--- |
| `config.jl`, `cli.jl`, `ctl.jl` | TOML configuration, and the two `ArgParse` command lines (`similarity-search`, `similarity-search-admin`) |
| `cli_handlers.jl`, `ctl_handlers.jl` | one function per subcommand: `build`, `search`, `searchbatch`, `allknn`, `fft`, `neardup`, `hsp`, `closestpair`, `describe`, `rebuild`, `dump`, `load` |
| `server.jl` | the HTTP API (Oxygen), one `EmbeddedEngine` per dataset, and the request/response mapping |
| `jobs.jl`, `executors.jl` | the job spool: an atomic directory tree (`queued/`, `running/`, `completed/`, `failed/`) of `.job.toml` files, dispatched as independent Julia subprocesses |
| `tokens.jl`, `telemetry.jl`, `cursors.jl` | access tokens, the `op_log` operation history, and server-side result cursors for pagination |
| `interactive.jl` | guided invocation through `REPL.TerminalMenus` |
| `apps/` | the three installable app entry points |

The schema, the persistence layer, the index engine and project management are not part of this
package. They are `SimilaritySearchEngine.Schema`, `.Persistence`, `.IndexEngine` and
`.Project`.

## 2. How a dataset is held

The server holds one `SimilaritySearchEngine.EmbeddedEngine` per dataset identifier, in
`AppState.handles`. That handle contains the two parts of a project, its RocksDB metadata store
and its search engine, which keeps them consistent across a restart. `reload_datasets!` opens
every dataset under `<workdir>/datasets/` with `open_project`, and a reopened dataset preserves
its index, its text profile, its staged items and its deletion marks.

There is no snapshot file. Earlier versions of this package wrote one JLD2 snapshot per dataset
and read it on demand, because the engine did not store its own index. The engine stores it
now, and a dataset is the directory that contains it.

**A job that operates on an entire dataset runs as a subprocess and opens its project in
read-only mode**, because the serving process may hold the project open, and the RocksDB write
lock is exclusive per process.

## 3. Kinds of project

The parameter `index_kind` of the API names a pair: the type of data a project holds, and the structure that indexes it:

| `index_kind` | engine | backend | notes |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `searchgraph` | `DenseEngine` | `SearchGraph` | approximate, adjusts its own parameters; the default |
| `exhaustive_search` | `DenseEngine` | `ExhaustiveSearch` | exact, linear scan |
| `parallel_exhaustive_search` | `DenseEngine` | `ParallelExhaustiveSearch` | exact, data-parallel |
| `bm25_invfile` | `FullTextEngine` | `BM25InvertedFile` | BM25 scoring |
| `invfile` | `FullTextEngine` | `TextInvertedFile` | TF-IDF cosine |
| `sparse_invfile` | `SparseEngine` | `InvertedFile` | sparse vectors encoded by the caller; requires `dimension` |

A text project is created with `FitFromCorpus`. Its vocabulary is fitted from the documents the
dataset has received when `index!` is called for the first time. Sending a pre-computed text
profile to the server is not available over HTTP.

## 4. REST API (base endpoints)

Every response of this API is JSON. A response that succeeded carries `status`; one that
failed carries `error` and `kind` (section 5). The bodies below are real responses, not
sketches.

Two names appear throughout and mean opposite things in two places. In a **search result**,
`id` is the identifier the caller gave the item and `doc_id` is the internal one the engine
assigned. In a **stored record** (`/fetch`, the operation log), `doc_id` is the caller's and
`_id` is the internal one. The inversion in search results is older than the rest of the API
and has not been corrected.

### Control

- `GET /healthz` — the process answers HTTP.
- `GET /readyz` — the process is ready to serve. `{"status":"ok"}`.
- `GET /metrics` — metrics in Prometheus text format: documents and deleted records per
  dataset, jobs in progress, and the counters the operation log feeds — requests per dataset
  and operation, distance computations, items inserted, and a histogram of request durations.

The counters cover the running process and start at zero when it starts, which is what a
Prometheus counter is expected to do; `simsearch_process_start_time_seconds` reports when
that was. They are accumulated as each request is recorded, not read back from the operation
log: a collector polls every few seconds, and reading a column family that grows with every
request would cost more than the requests it measures. The log remains the durable record and
is read through `GET /api/v1/datasets/{id}/log`.

### Datasets

- `POST /api/v1/datasets` — creates one. Accepts `id`, `index_kind` (see section 3),
  `distance`, `dimension`, the join-group fields `join_group`, `holds_metadata`, `key`, and
  an optional `meta_schema`. Answers `201`.
- `GET /api/v1/datasets?offset=&limit=` — every dataset on disk, loaded or not.
- `GET /api/v1/datasets/{id}` — one of them.
- `DELETE /api/v1/datasets/{id}` — destroys it.
- `POST /api/v1/admin/datasets/{id}/unload` and `/reload` — closes or reopens a dataset
  without restarting the server. The `rebuild` subcommand of the command line requires this,
  because the RocksDB write lock is exclusive per process.

```json
POST /api/v1/datasets          {"status":"created","id":"ds"}
DELETE /api/v1/datasets/{id}   {"status":"deleted","id":"ds"}
POST .../unload                {"status":"unloaded","id":"ds"}
POST .../reload                {"status":"reloaded","id":"ds"}

GET /api/v1/datasets/{id}
{"id":"ds", "index_kind":"searchgraph", "distance":"L2",
 "created_at":"2026-09-14T19:41:57.059", "loaded":true,
 "doc_count":5, "tombstone_count":0, "tombstone_ratio":0,
 "join_group":null, "holds_metadata":false, "key":null,
 "meta_schema":[{"name":"year","type":"int64"}],
 "beamsearch_baseline":{"bsize":4,"delta":1,"maxvisits":1000000}}
```

`GET /api/v1/datasets` wraps a list of those objects: `{"status":"ok", "datasets":[...],
"total":2, "offset":0, "limit":2}`. `doc_count`, `tombstone_count`, `tombstone_ratio`,
`meta_schema` and `beamsearch_baseline` are reported for a dataset that is open;
`beamsearch_baseline` is `null` for one that is not backed by a graph, and `meta_schema` is
`null` for one that declares nothing.

`meta_schema` declares which fields of an item's metadata the dataset expects and what each
one holds:

```json
{"id": "papers", "index_kind": "bm25_invfile",
 "meta_schema": [{"name": "year", "type": "int64"},
                 {"name": "published", "type": "timestamp"}]}
```

The types are `string`, `int64`, `float64`, `bool` and `timestamp`. An append is refused with
`400` when a declared field carries another type. Declaring is additive: a field that is not
declared is stored as it arrives, and a dataset that declares nothing behaves as before. The
declared fields are not indexed; what the declaration changes is that a filter compares in
the declared type, so a `timestamp` is compared as an instant rather than as the text that
stores it. The engine holds the declaration inside the project, which is why it survives a
restart and travels with `dump`.

- `GET /api/v1/datasets/{id}/join_group` — the datasets tagged with the same `join_group`.

```json
{"join_group":"g",
 "members":[{"index_uuid":"txt","index_kind":"bm25_invfile","key":"body","holds_metadata":true}]}
```

### Search and indexing

- `POST /api/v1/datasets/{id}/append` — inserts items. A dense item contains `vector`, a text
  item contains `text`, and a sparse item contains `indices` and `values`. The fields
  `doc_id`, `keywords` and `refs`, and any other field, become the metadata of the item.
- `POST /api/v1/datasets/{id}/search` — dense and sparse search, with optional `filter`,
  `page_size` and `beamsearch_overrides`.
- `POST /api/v1/datasets/{id}/ftsearch` — text search.
- `POST /api/v1/datasets/{id}/fetch` and `GET /api/v1/datasets/{id}/exists?ids=` — records by
  identifier, and whether an identifier exists.
- `POST /api/v1/datasets/{id}/delete` — logical deletion.
- `POST /api/v1/datasets/{id}/calibrate` — recall calibration for a graph-backed project.
- `POST /api/v1/search/hybrid` and `POST /api/v1/search/group` — reciprocal rank fusion over
  two datasets, and a text query sent to every dataset of a join group.

```json
POST .../append     {"status":"appended","id":"ds","inserted":5}
POST .../delete     {"status":"soft_deleted","id":"ds","doc_id":1}
POST .../calibrate  {"status":"calibrated","id":"ds",
                     "baseline":{"bsize":4,"delta":1,"maxvisits":1000000}}

POST .../search  and  POST .../ftsearch
{"status":"searched","id":"ds",
 "results":[{"id":"d1","doc_id":1,"distance":0},
            {"id":"d2","doc_id":2,"distance":1}]}

POST .../fetch
{"status":"fetched","id":"ds",
 "results":[{"id":"d1","doc_id":"d1","_id":1,"keywords":["k1"],"refs":[],
             "schema_version":1,"year":2021}]}

GET .../exists?ids=d1,nope
{"status":"ok","id":"ds",
 "results":[{"id":"d1","exists":true,"deleted":false},
            {"id":"nope","exists":false,"deleted":false}]}

POST /api/v1/search/hybrid
{"status":"searched","results":[{"id":"d1","doc_id":1,"score":0.0327}]}

POST /api/v1/search/group
{"status":"searched","join_group":"g",
 "results":{"body":[{"id":"t1","doc_id":1,"score":-0.267}]}}
```

A `fetch` result merges the item's metadata into the record, which is why `year` sits beside
`keywords` above. A `search` over a text dataset reports a BM25 score with its sign inverted,
under the name `distance`, which is the convention of the library: a smaller value is a closer
match. A filtered search that could not fill `k` adds `"insufficient_results":true`, since it
reads a bounded number of candidates before applying the filter.

An operation on one dataset is addressed under that dataset. The two queries that read more
than one are under `/api/v1/search/`, which is the only place where a route is not about a
single dataset. The earlier prefix `/api/v1/simsearch/` was removed on 2026-09-13: it marked a
distinction that the API stopped making.

### Vocabulary

- `GET /api/v1/datasets/{id}/vocab?scan=&sample=` — what a text dataset's vocabulary covers.

```json
{"id":"txt", "vocsize":3, "trainsize":3, "numtokens":9, "avgdoclen":3,
 "top_tokens":[{"token":"gato","ndocs":3,"occs":3}],
 "queries":1, "query_tokens":1, "query_oov_tokens":0, "query_oov_rate":0}
```

With `scan=true`, six more fields:

```json
{"live_tokens":9, "live_oov_tokens":0, "live_oov_rate":0,
 "live_documents_scanned":3, "live_documents_total":3, "live_sampled":false}
```

A vocabulary is fitted once and does not grow. The rate over the queries says the words being
asked for are missing, and the rate over the documents says the words the dataset already
holds are missing; the second is what `rebuild` corrects, by refitting the vocabulary over
the documents the dataset has now.

The query counters cost nothing and are always reported. The reading over the documents is
asked for with `scan=true`, and it is bounded: at most `sample` documents are read, spread
evenly over the dataset, and `live_sampled` says whether it read all of them. The default
sample takes about a second whatever the dataset's size; `sample=0` reads every document,
which on a large dataset takes minutes and is better asked for offline with `describe`.
`409` for a dataset that holds no text or was never indexed.

### Telemetry

- `GET /api/v1/datasets/{id}/log?offset=&limit=` — the dataset's `op_log`: one record per
  `search`, `ftsearch`, `append` or `delete`.

```json
{"status":"ok","total":4,"offset":0,"limit":1,
 "entries":[{"operation":"delete","timestamp":"2026-09-14T19:42:11.195",
             "details":{"index_uuid":"ds","doc_id":1,"token":null}}]}
```

A `search` entry carries more in `details`: `distance_name`, `dimension`,
`distance_evaluations` and `elapsed_seconds`; an `append` entry carries `items_inserted`.

The number of distance computations of a search is obtained from the engine, in a
`SimilaritySearchEngine.SearchStats` instance that `_run_search` passes to `search` and to
`ftsearch`. It is not obtained by reading a context before and after the call: a search uses a
context taken from a pool of the engine, so a counter read from this package includes the work
of any other search executed since. For `append` the second method is correct, because an
insertion uses the engine's own context under an exclusive write lock.

### Asynchronous jobs

- `POST /api/v1/jobs/{kind}` — enqueues a job (`allknn`, `fft`, `neardup`, `hsp`,
  `searchbatch`, `closestpair`, `build`, `dump`, `load`). Answers `202`.
- `GET /api/v1/jobs?offset=&limit=`, `GET /api/v1/jobs/{job_id}` and `/result` — the jobs,
  the state of one, and its output.
- `POST /api/v1/jobs/{job_id}/block`, `/resume`, `/kill`, and `DELETE /api/v1/jobs/{job_id}`.
- `POST /api/v1/admin/jobs/gc` — removes the jobs and cursors that have expired.

```json
POST /api/v1/jobs/allknn  [202]   {"status":"accepted","job_id":"fe3198116091f825"}

GET /api/v1/jobs
{"status":"ok","total":1,"offset":0,"limit":1,
 "jobs":[{"id":"fe3198116091f825","kind":"allknn","status":"queued"}]}

POST /api/v1/admin/jobs/gc
{"status":"ok","jobs_purged":[],"cursors_purged":[],"cursors_expired":[]}
```

A job's state is `queued`, `running`, `blocked`, `completed` or `failed`.
`GET /api/v1/jobs/{job_id}/result` streams the file the job wrote, except for `dump`, whose
result is a directory: for that one it answers `{"bundle_dir": ..., "manifest": {...}}`.

### Tokens

- `POST /api/v1/admin/tokens` — creates one. Accepts `user`, `permissions` and an optional
  `expires_at`.
- `GET /api/v1/admin/tokens` — every token stored, expired or not.
- `DELETE /api/v1/admin/tokens/{token}` — revokes one.
- `POST /api/v1/admin/tokens/prune` — removes the expired ones.

```json
POST /api/v1/admin/tokens  [201]
{"status":"created","token":"703ffec26b6db7b1...","permissions":["read:*"]}

GET /api/v1/admin/tokens
{"status":"ok",
 "tokens":[{"token":"703ffec26b6db7b1...","user":"alice","permissions":["read:*"],
            "created_at":"2026-09-14T19:42:20.595","expires_at":null}]}

DELETE /api/v1/admin/tokens/{token}   {"status":"revoked"}
POST /api/v1/admin/tokens/prune       {"status":"ok","pruned":0}
```

The token string is returned once, when it is created. `GET /api/v1/admin/tokens` is an audit
listing and reports them in full, which is why it requires `admin`.

### Authentication

Every `/api/v1` endpoint requires a token when `[auth] enabled` is true in `config.toml`.
`/healthz`, `/readyz` and `/metrics` answer without one, so a supervisor and a metrics
collector work without credentials. The default is `false`, which is the behavior of a server
that has never had authentication.

The token travels in the `Authorization` header, as `Bearer <token>` or as the bare token.
A permission is `operation:dataset`:

| operation | grants | includes |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `read` | the queries and the `GET` endpoints | — |
| `write` | append, delete, calibrate, job submission | `read` |
| `admin` | dataset creation and deletion, the token endpoints, job control, the operation log | `write` and `read` |

`dataset` is a dataset id or `*`. A route that is not about one dataset — listing datasets,
the job endpoints, the token endpoints, `/api/v1/search/group` — requires the operation over
`*`, so a token restricted to one dataset uses that dataset and cannot enumerate the rest.
`admin:*` grants everything. A request without a valid token is answered `401`; a valid token
without the permission is answered `403`, and the body names the permission that was required.

The first token is created against the working directory, because a server with
authentication enabled refuses to start while no token exists, and the endpoint that creates
tokens is itself behind authentication:

```bash
similarity-search add-token --user admin --permissions "admin:*" --workdir ./workdir
```

Later tokens are created with `POST /api/v1/admin/tokens` or with `similarity-search-ctl
add-token`, which is the same endpoint. A token may carry an `expires_at`, an ISO 8601
timestamp that is verified when the token is created and again on every request.

## 5. How failures are reported

The engine raises typed errors. This package maps them **by category**, never by the text of the message:

| engine category | HTTP | CLI exit code |
| :--- | ---: | ---: |
| `NotFound` | 404 | 4 |
| `ConflictingState` (staged backlog, untrained profile, empty project) | 409 | 5 |
| `InvalidRequest` (wrong payload, wrong dimension, bad option) | 400 | 2 |
| `StorageFailure` | 500 | 70 |

Two status codes come from this package rather than from the engine: `401` when a request
carries no valid token, and `403` when its token lacks the permission the route requires.

An error response contains two fields: `error`, the message, intended for a person, and `kind`,
the concrete engine type, intended for a client that selects a behavior. Failures detected by a
command line itself, such as a dataset directory that does not exist or an input file that
cannot be read, return exit code `1`. They are detected before the engine is called.

## 6. Configuration

`config.toml` (or `.similarity-search-server.toml`):

```toml
[paths]
workdir = "./workdir"

[server]
host = "127.0.0.1"
port = 8080

[resources]
query_threads_pct = 80
batch_threads_pct = 20
```

`[resources]` divides this server's threads between answering queries and executing jobs. A
job runs as its own process, so the reserved share is spent as a number of processes and a
number of threads each: at most four jobs at once, each with its part of
`floor(threads × batch_threads_pct / 100)`, and never more than that share in total. The
remaining threads stay with the server. `serve` prints the resulting numbers when it starts,
for example `at most 4 concurrent job(s), 3 thread(s) each (20.0% of this server's 64
thread(s))`.

The number of threads the server itself has is the one given to Julia when it starts
(`julia -t auto`), not a value in this file.

## 7. Tests

Two levels, selected with `test_args=["full"]` or `SSE_TEST_LEVEL=full`:

- **light** (50 assertions, approximately 5 s): the interface with the engine. It verifies the
  mapping from the names used in requests to engine types, from engine errors to status codes
  and exit codes, and from the items of a request to engine items. No server is started and no
  subprocess is created. This level detects a change in the engine on the day it is made.
- **full** (585 assertions, approximately 19 minutes): the end-to-end suites for the API, the
  jobs and the command lines. They start servers and execute subprocesses. Near the end, the
  run produces no output for about ten minutes, while the command-line suite waits for jobs to
  expire. The run has not stopped.

```bash
julia --project=server -e 'using Pkg; Pkg.develop(path="."); Pkg.test()'
julia --project=server -e 'using Pkg; Pkg.test(test_args=["full"])'
```
